title: Where the edges came from
intro: The level above named the four statistics, the block matrix and the one lens-free check. This level takes each apart: what shape a curve would have without a band, why the fourth statistic may be the cause of the other three rather than a fourth witness, what the block matrix does and does not license, and how much of the onset the ambiguity sweep actually fixes.

chapters.title: Four curves and one denominator
chapters.body:
The band claim is not that the four statistics of [[workspace-boundary-metrics]] are high in the middle of the model. It is that each of them bends at roughly the same depth, near layer 38, and bends again near layer 92.

Without a band, each curve would take a different shape. [[lens-next-token-accuracy]] would climb steadily with depth, since a later layer sits closer to the output and should agree with it more often; what [[fig-28]] shows instead is a floor near zero, a tick up, a slow rise, then a steep jump in the last few layers. [[readout-excess-kurtosis]] would hold a constant value if readouts were equally peaked at every depth, rather than sitting near the Gaussian value of zero through the first third and then rising ([[kurtosis]]). [[top1-autocorrelation]] would hold a constant margin over its [[position-shuffled-null]]. The fraction in [[j-space-effective-dimensionality]] would be flat.

All four are read off the same operation. The [[j-lens-readout]] is $\mathrm{softmax}(W_U\,\mathrm{norm}(J_\ell h_\ell))$, with $J_\ell$ the [[averaged-jacobian]] for that layer.

Panel (d) reports that in the early layers $J_\ell$ confines the lens vectors to a small subspace. A readout built from a low-rank $J_\ell$ has little room to move: its logits stay close to a bell, so excess kurtosis stays near zero; it rarely puts the model's own top-1 token near the front; and it varies only along the few directions that survive, so persistence across positions stays near the null.

The fourth panel is therefore not a fourth witness. It is closer to a cause of the other three.

The paper reports the same low rank from another direction. Through layers 0 to 33 no two of the three lenses agree on their readouts, and the J-lens vectors are nearly orthogonal to those of the [[logit-lens]] and the [[tuned-lens]] — which the paper attributes to that same confinement.

chapters.title: The block matrix, and the layers it skips
chapters.body:
[[cka]] works on relations rather than on vectors. At one layer, all of the [[jacobian-lens]] vectors are collected and the matrix of pairwise similarities among them is formed. The same is done at a second layer. The two matrices are then compared.

Because only the pattern of similarities enters, rotating a whole layer's dictionary registers as no change at all. What registers is a change in which tokens sit near which.

Run over every pair of layers, the comparison gives three blocks: an early one covering roughly the first third of the model, a long middle one, and a small late one. That is the picture [[fig-27]] draws.

The matrix by itself says only that three regimes exist. It does not say which of them holds the [[j-space]] content the paper is after, so two anchors are supplied from outside it. The final layer's lens vectors must encode next-token predictions, since at that depth the readout is essentially the [[unembedding-matrix]] applied to the state the model is about to decode. The first layer's vectors cannot carry much, since the first layer can only encode the identity of the present token. The middle block is what is left, and the paper reads it as the [[workspace-layers]].

The argument is one of elimination, and it is only as strong as those two anchors.

Two qualifications come from the paper itself. In some models the transition is more gradual and sometimes contains sub-blocks, so the three-way split is not uniform across the models tested. And the analysis runs on [[layer-subsampling]]: the matrix is computed at a subset of layers, so the finest boundary it can draw is the gap between two sampled layers. A change spread over the layers in between arrives as one step.

chapters.title: Two readings of an empty first third
chapters.body:
The paper puts two accounts of the empty first third side by side and does not choose between them.

On the first, the early [[residual-stream]] genuinely carries no linearly accessible, causally relevant content of the kind the model could put into words ([[verbal-report]]). What it carries instead is low-level parsing work that the paper elsewhere finds outside the workspace, and content worth broadcasting takes some depth to form. The paper draws the parallel to [[global-workspace-theory]], where workspace contents in the brain require a stretch of recurrent processing before ignition. Calling those layers [[sensory-layers]] assumes this reading.

On the second, [[early-layer-lens-degeneracy]], the content is present and the instrument cannot resolve it. The mechanism is specific. The Jacobian used at layer $\ell$ is averaged over the path from that layer to the final one. For an early layer that path is almost the whole network, and the [[local-linearization]] the method rests on is at its weakest across so much nonlinearity. A direction that matters early can fail to survive the average.

Nothing in the section decides between the two. The block structure establishes the early layers as a coherent regime of their own, which both accounts predict.

One circumstantial point does not settle it either: the logit lens and the tuned lens produce nothing meaningful at those depths, but all three lenses read the residual stream through the output vocabulary, so their common silence is consistent with a common blind spot.

The paper states the consequence plainly. Parts of the model's true workspace, not captured by the lens, may operate in layers earlier than the ones the analysis names.

chapters.title: The sweep that does not use the lens
chapters.body:
One measurement at the onset does not pass through the lens at all.

The construction is small and fully specified ([[embedding-mixture-experiment]]). Sixteen pairs of single-token country names are used, in forty carrier sentences of the form "My sister has always wanted to visit ___". At the concept token's position the input embedding is replaced by $(1-\alpha)\,e_B + \alpha\,e_A$. For each trial $\alpha$ is swept from 0 to 1, and the [[activations]] at that position are recorded at every layer.

The readout is a ratio between the model's own runs. The trial at $\alpha = 0$ and the trial at $\alpha = 1$ give two points at that position and layer. Any intermediate activation is placed on the line joining them, and [[projection-share]] is how far along that line it sits. At the two ends the value is 0 and 1 by construction.

No Jacobian and no vocabulary enter. Each trial supplies its own axis, so no structure is imposed across prompts.

Through the early layers the share varies smoothly with $\alpha$, tracking the input mixture roughly proportionally. From about layer 38 it instead sits near one endpoint or the other and switches between them at a threshold value of $\alpha$, and the boundary stays similarly sharp at every layer after that. Sharp commitment at threshold is the shape [[ignition]] predicts ([[fig-29]]).

The same figure adds a lens-side view. The rank of whichever of the two concepts the lens ranks higher is recorded at each layer: very early, neither ranks highly; a few layers in, both appear for unambiguous inputs but not for ambiguous ones; by layer 38 they appear even at maximal ambiguity. Restricting the projection share to the component along the two concepts' [[j-lens-vector]] directions reproduces the lens-free panel.

chapters.title: How sharp, and what it does not reach
chapters.body:
The appendix quantifies how abrupt the switch is. For each prompt, [[transition-width]] is the change in $\alpha$ needed to move the projection share from 10% to 90%. Early in the model the width is large. It then falls steeply over roughly layers 21 through 42 ([[fig-70]]).

Layer 38 sits inside that decline rather than at a break in it. The sweep supports an onset somewhere in that window; it does not independently pick out the layer the lens statistics named.

The figure's other comparison is lens-defined. The activation is split into its component along the two concepts' lens vectors and the complement left after projecting out the top sixteen lens vectors. The first sharpens more and reaches its floor earlier. That is a claim about the J-space specifically, and it is made with the instrument in question.

A further check goes to per-trial behavior ([[fig-71]]). At the $\alpha$ where the input leans least toward either concept, an activation that merely reflected its input would put every trial near 0.5. Early layers do that. By halfway through the depth the J-space component has split toward 0 and 1 while its complement still has mass at 0.5; by mid-band both are split. The average is ambiguous because individual trials commit, not because activations sit in between.

All of this bears on the onset. The late edge has nothing comparable. The argument there is [[jacobian-approaches-identity]]: as $J_\ell$ approaches the identity the readout collapses toward the plain unembedding projection, which is also what the second rise in the dimensionality curve records — the lens inheriting the unembedding's full rank.

That is a statement about the instrument as much as about those layers. Naming them [[motor-layers]] treats it as a statement about the model, and whether they still hold content the lens can no longer tell apart from the imminent output is not tested. [[layer-bands]] carries the paper's own wording of the split.
